page.layout: Two medallion portraits with legends at the top, centred; below them one column of running text with two paragraphs. The running head sits at the top, the page number at the top left.

main_text.l: [?] TARQVINIVS PRI[?]
[?] CVS
TANAQVIL
TARQVIN
TARQVINIVS Priscus qui prius Lucumo, Romano-
rum rex quintus, imperauit Romanis anno mundi 3349. ante
Christum natum 613. apud Ancum Martium liberaliter dex-
tréque obeundo officia, in familiarem venit amicitiam, vt pu-
blicis ac priuatis consiliis bello,domíque interesset, & per om-
nia expertus postremo tutor etiam liberis Regis, testamento
instituieretur.mortuo Anco, instituit hic vt quàm primum co-
mitia Regi creando fierent,quibus indictis,sub tempus pueros
regios venatum ablegauit:& primus petiffe ambitiosè regnum
& orationem habuiffe ad conciliandos plebis animos compo-
sitam fertur:maximè verò cùm Tatium Sabinum,etiam ex ho-
ste Regem factum diceret,ac inculcaret,populus eum regnare
iuffit. numerum Senatorum & equitū duplicauit: Circum Ro-
mae aedificauit, ludos Romanos instituit magnificos: Sabinos
vicit: Latinos priscos domuit: primus triumphans Romae in-
trauit:muros & cloacas fecit: Capitolium inchoauit. Tandem
à filiis Anci Martij, cui in regno succesferat, interfectus est 37.
imperij anno. his temporibus Ierusalem à Nabuchodonosore
capta ac euersa est:& Massilia condita. Consulito lib.1.Eutrop.
Diony.Halicar.lib.3. Titum Liuium lib.1.deca.1.
TANAQVIL, Tarquinij Prisci vxor fuit, perita, vt vul-
go Etrusci, coelestium prodigiorum mulier. Hæc cùm aquila
suspensis demissa leniter alis pileum viri abstuliffet, rursúsque
velut ministerio diuinitus missa, capiti aptè repofuiffet, hæc
inquam, virum complexa,alta sperare iuffit. id siquidè factum
est ipsis primò Romam ingredientibus,antequam regnaret ipse
Tarquinius Priscus. Vide vt supra.

page.notes: The two medallion portraits are illustrations, not text. Their legends are set in the coin rims and are only partly legible: the left medallion shows a bearded figure with legend fragments reading "TARQVINIVS PRI" and "CVS"; the right medallion shows a female bust with legend "TANAQVIL" and "TARQVIN". The exact letters at the rim edges are uncertain and are marked [?]. No marginal notes, catchword or signature are printed on this page.
